[Celine Dubois]: Members of the board, I find the evidence overwhelmingly in favor of granting parole in this case. The applicant's risk assessment score of 2/10 indicates a low risk of re-offending, supported by a five-year clean conduct record within the institution.  They have actively participated in vocational training, secured stable employment post-release, and have a strong support system in place. These factors, combined with the nature of their non-violent offense, demonstrate the applicant has successfully rehabilitated and poses minimal risk to public safety. 


Therefore, I recommend granting parole based on a thorough review of the statutory criteria.

[Adam Volkov]: Members of the board, I agree with Ms. Dubois' assessment. The applicant's risk score of 2/10, coupled with their five-year clean conduct record, strongly suggests a low risk of re-offending. Their participation in vocational training, secure employment offer, and strong family support demonstrate successful rehabilitation and a commitment to reintegration.  All statutory criteria, including risk assessment, conduct, rehabilitation, and release plan, are met in this case.  Therefore, I recommend granting parole.
